3.happening: We drop the new interval into the list.
3.why: Once it is just another interval, the standard merge handles it.
3.invariant: The list now contains every interval to be merged.

4.happening: We sort all intervals by their start value.
4.why: Sorting puts overlapping intervals next to each other.
4.invariant: Intervals are now in non-decreasing start order.

5.happening: We start merged as an empty list.
5.why: It collects the final, non-overlapping intervals.
5.invariant: No interval has been merged yet.

6.why: Each interval is considered once, left to right.
6.invariant: All intervals before i are already merged into the result.

7.happening: We read the current interval's start = {start}.
7.why: The start decides whether it overlaps the last kept interval.
7.invariant: start belongs to the highlighted interval i.

8.happening: We read the current interval's end = {end}.
8.why: The end may extend the last merged interval.
8.invariant: [start, end] is exactly the highlighted interval.

9.happening: merged is empty, so this interval opens the result.
9.why: The first interval has nothing to overlap.
9.invariant: The result always begins with the smallest-start interval.

9.happening: merged already has intervals, so we compare against the last one.
9.why: Only the most recent kept interval can overlap the current one.
9.invariant: Intervals are sorted, so earlier ones can no longer overlap.

10.happening: We append [{start}, {end}] as the first merged interval.
10.invariant: merged now holds exactly one interval.

12.happening: We read last_end = {last_end}, the end of the last merged interval.
12.why: Overlap is decided by comparing start against last_end.
12.invariant: last_end is the right edge of the current merged block.

13.happening: start {start} is beyond last_end {last_end} — no overlap.
13.why: A gap means this interval is a separate block.

13.happening: start {start} is not beyond last_end {last_end} — they overlap.
13.why: The current interval touches or dips into the last block.
13.invariant: Overlapping intervals fuse into one block.

14.happening: We append [{start}, {end}] as a new disjoint block.
14.why: There is a gap before it, so it stands alone.
14.invariant: merged blocks never overlap each other.

16.why: The overlap reaches further right, so the block must grow.
16.invariant: A block's end only ever increases.

16.happening: end {end} is within last_end {last_end}, so nothing changes.
16.why: This interval is fully covered by the last block.
16.invariant: A contained interval is absorbed without changing the block.

17.happening: We stretch the last block's end to {end}.
17.why: The overlapping interval reached further than the block did.
17.invariant: The merged block now covers both intervals.

18.why: Every interval, including the inserted one, has been placed.
18.invariant: merged is sorted and has no overlaps.

init.happening: Insert the new interval, sort, and prepare an empty result.
init.why: Turns insertion into a plain merge.
init.invariant: All intervals are sorted; none merged yet.

loop.invariant: Intervals before i are already merged.

update.happening: Read an interval or grow the result.
update.why: Each interval is appended or fused.

return.invariant: The result is sorted and overlap-free.
